mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate trend over the past 3 months signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 5.0%, it indicates a weakening labor market that typically leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of CPIAUCSL above 228.0 and FEDFUNDS above 0.15% signals a monetary policy response to inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 228.0 and FEDFUNDS > 0.15, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 1.0% for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to higher discount rates and reduced liquidity, producing negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS > 1.0% for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past 6 months indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS increasing for at least 6 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 700,000 units, it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST < 700.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 97.0 and a concurrent decline in real GDP (GDPC1 below 13400) signals a weakening supply chain and economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where INDPRO < 97.0 and GDPC1 < 13400, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime (INDPRO falling below 97.0 for 3 consecutive months), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to reduced production capacity and higher input costs, producing negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO < 97.0 for 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
